terms.gloss: hug, hold in one’s arms, cuddle
evidence: Plaut. Asin. 619: num fūmus est haec mulier quam amplexāre?
Plaut. Asin. 739: patrem hanc amplexārī tuom?
terms.comment: The frequentative of amplector: mostly ante-classical and in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Liv. 36.17: ōceanus, quī orbem terrārum amplexū fīnit (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: an embrace, a clasp; an encircling
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.1.7: ē complexū parentum abreptōs fīliōs ad necem dūcere (Lewis & Short)
Cic. ND 2.58: omnia complexū suō coërcet et continet (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Ere, salvē. Sed num fūmus est haec mulier quam amplexāre?
phrases.english: Hello, master. But is that woman you’re hugging made of smoke?

phrases.latin: ōceanus, quī orbem terrārum amplexū fīnit
phrases.english: the ocean, which bounds the circle of the earth with its embrace

phrases.latin: ō quī complexūs et gaudia quanta fuērunt
phrases.english: oh, what embraces there were, and what joy

sources: Lewis & Short: amplector · Lewis & Short: complector · Lewis & Short: amplexor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 330.
